cf.title: Don't use the deprecated and insecure PQcancel in our frontend tools anymore

input.subject: Don't use the deprecated and insecure PQcancel in our frontend tools anymore

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal or the overall design. The only surviving objection, prior-attempts-1, is a fixable portability point: v13-0003 uses pselect() behind an existence check, and [P12] records that some platforms shipped a pselect() that did not work. A committer who knows the frontend signal and portability code can settle that, and the 1 second select() fallback already exists.

brief.title: Frontend tools send encrypted cancel requests from a dedicated thread
brief.problem: psql, pg_dump, pgbench, vacuumdb and other frontend tools still send cancel requests with PQcancel, which does not use encryption. So the cancel key travels in clear text even when the session uses SSL. The author wants all tools using fe_utils cancel handling to stop doing that.
brief.proposed_design: The tools switch to the newer libpq cancel API (61461a300), which uses the same encryption settings as the cancelled connection. That API is not signal-safe, so the SIGINT handler now wakes a dedicated cancel thread through a self-pipe, as Windows already does. SetCancelConn() and ResetCancelConn() wait for any in-flight cancel, and wait_on_slots() uses pselect() or a 1 second select() poll.
user_visible_surface: Cancel requests from psql, pg_dump, pg_restore, pgbench, pg_amcheck, clusterdb, reindexdb and vacuumdb now use the connection's SSL/GSS encryption.
psql -f scripts now stop with exit code 3 on Ctrl+C during \copy ... from pstdin, \prompt or \password input (committed as 0001).
With a stuck cancel connection, the psql prompt stays blocked until the cancel request finishes or times out.
fe_utils cancel.h API changes, including a new setup_cancel_handler() taking a signal callback and a thread callback.
New configure and meson check for pselect().
author_claims: PQcancel is insecure because it sends the cancel request without encryption.
The design makes cancel handling more uniform between Windows and Unix, and does not need changes at call sites.
The remaining race, where a late cancel hits a later query, comes from the cancel protocol and is unlikely in interactive use.
Backporting to PG17 and PG18 would be desirable as a security fix, but may be too large.
brief.thread_state: Heikki Linnakangas reviewed in depth, Zsolt Parragi, Anthonin Bonnefoy and Michael Paquier commented, and Peter Eisentraut committed v13-0001 and is reviewing the rest. Backpatching and Heikki's design ideas, such as cancel inside libpq and mutually exclusive callbacks, have no resolution.
unclear: No consensus on backpatching to PG17 and PG18.
The thread shows no test with a bad network for tools other than psql, such as pg_dump parallel workers.
No automated tests for the new thread-based cancel path are mentioned.
Behaviour when the cancel thread cannot be created, and on platforms without threads, is not described.
The material does not say whether calling setup_cancel_handler() twice is now guarded (Zsolt's point).

prior_attempts.title: Revert "Use pselect(2) not select(2), if available, to wait in postmaster's loop."
prior_attempts.quote: Buildfarm results suggest that some platforms have versions of pselect(2) that are not merely non-atomic, but flat out non-functional.
prior_attempts.reason:
This reverts commit 81069a9efc5a374dd39874a161f456f0fb3afba4.

Buildfarm results suggest that some platforms have versions of pselect(2)
that are not merely non-atomic, but flat out non-functional.  Revert the
use-pselect patch to confirm this diagnosis (and exclude the no-SA_RESTART
patch as the source of trouble).  If it's so, we should probably look into
blacklisting specific platforms that have broken pselect.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: This uses pselect() only in frontend wait_on_slots(), not in the postmaster, and falls back to select() with a 1 second timeout. The thread does not discuss how a broken pselect() would be detected.

prior_attempts.title: pgbench: allow to cancel queries during benchmark
prior_attempts.quote: Due to commit 61461a300c1c, this patch needs to be reworked.
prior_attempts.reason: Fabien COELHO said thread #0 cancelling clients that other threads manage can cause race conditions, and asked that each thread cancel its own clients. In message #19 the author found two more problems: thread #0 cannot cancel anything once it leaves its loop, and with -C each thread recreates its PGcancel objects while thread #0 reads them. Alvaro Herrera then said commit 61461a300c1c, which deprecated PQcancel, requires the patch to be reworked. The author planned a redesign, but the visible messages show no new version.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: That patch added Ctrl+C cancel for all pgbench clients and stopped because it had to move to the new cancel API. This proposal makes that move for fe_utils users but keeps one global cancel connection.

objections.title: pselect() was reverted before because some platforms ship a broken one
objections.failure_scenario: On a platform whose pselect() exists but does not work, configure detects it and wait_on_slots() uses it. Then vacuumdb -j or reindexdb -j can miss Ctrl+C or fail while it waits on its slots. The buildfarm or a user on that platform finds out after commit.
objections.argument: [P12] records that pselect() in the postmaster loop was reverted because some platforms' versions "are not merely non-atomic, but flat out non-functional". v13-0003 makes the first use of pselect() since then, behind a plain configure check (message #22 notes it is unused today). The thread does not say whether those platforms are still supported or how a broken pselect() would be detected. The 1 second select() fallback already exists, so a narrower or opt-in use is a possible way out.
objections.author_must_show: Which platforms had the broken pselect() behind the earlier revert, and are any of them still supported or in the buildfarm today?

precedents.title: Revert "Use pselect(2) not select(2), if available, to wait in postmaster's loop."

critic.reasoning: [P12] is about the postmaster loop, but its recorded reason, a pselect() that does not work on some platforms, applies to any caller. The thread does not say whether those platforms are still supported, and message #27 chose pselect() without discussing this.

refuted.title: Cancel can now fail where the plaintext cancel used to succeed
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs a long query in psql over a GSS-encrypted or certificate-verified SSL connection, and the Kerberos ticket or client certificate expires mid-session. On Ctrl+C the new cancel connection fails its handshake and the query keeps running, where PQcancel would have stopped it. The user learns this only from a "Could not send cancel request" line.
refuted.argument: The patch makes every cancel open a fresh connection with the session's own encryption settings (message #1, 0005 commit message). Before, the cancel needed only a reachable port and the cancel key. Neither the thread nor the commit messages say what happens when the encrypted handshake fails while the main session is still healthy, or whether the tools then report the failure or fall back. Message #11 already names a pooler in the path as a realistic setup, and it is a second place where the cancel path and the session path can differ.
refuted.author_must_show: When the encrypted cancel handshake fails but the session is healthy, what do psql and pg_dump do, and is that loss of a working cancel accepted on purpose?

critic.reasoning: Message #9 shows psql reporting a failed cancel with "Could not send cancel request" while the session continues. A fallback to a cleartext cancel would undo the purpose of the patch, and the handshake rule comes from the libpq API already committed in 61461a300.

refuted.title: Backport to 17 and 18 would change client behaviour in a minor release
refuted.failure_scenario: A site updates to a 17.x minor release. A script run with psql -f now exits with code 3 on Ctrl+C at a \copy prompt. Its psql prompt can also stay blocked on a stuck cancel connection, and cancels through its proxy start to fail. The site finds out during an incident, after a release that promised only fixes.
refuted.argument: Message #1 and the brief keep backpatching open as a security fix, and nothing in the thread settles it. The series includes user-visible changes: the exit-code change (0001, message #28), a new pselect() configure check, and a new thread in every frontend tool. Message #9 also shows the prompt waiting on a stuck cancel. A committer would likely want the backpatch question decided before commit, because the threat model of a cleartext cancel key decides whether these changes are justified in stable branches.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the plan master-only, and if a backport is still wanted, which parts would go back and without which behaviour changes?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 already calls a backport probably unrealistic and only asks for opinions, and no one in the thread supports one. The scenario needs a backport that nobody has proposed in concrete form, and the commit to master does not depend on it.

refuted.title: New pselect() dependency repeats a reverted approach without a guard
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs vacuumdb --jobs=8 or reindexdb on a platform where configure finds pselect() but the function does not work. Ctrl+C either hangs in wait_on_slots() or is ignored until a socket wakes up. The user finds out only when interrupting a long maintenance run.
refuted.argument: 0003 adds the first use of pselect() in the tree, behind a new configure and meson check that only tests whether the function exists. [P12] records that the backend's switch to pselect() was reverted because some platforms had versions that were "flat out non-functional". Message #22 listed ppoll(), already used in pgbench, as an alternative. Message #27 chose pselect() without discussing that history.
refuted.author_must_show: Which platforms is the pselect() path tested on, and what stops a present but broken pselect() from being chosen over the 1-second select() fallback?

precedents.title: Revert "Use pselect(2) not select(2), if available, to wait in postmaster's loop."

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1, which states the same pselect() concern with the same precedent and a more focused question.

refuted.title: Thread-based cancel path has no automated test
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch changes a SetCancelConn() caller or a psql siglongjmp() target. The cancel thread then deadlocks waiting on an in-flight cancel, or the signal reaches the wrong thread. No regression test fails, and users report a hung psql prompt after release.
refuted.argument: All checks shown in the thread are manual: iptables and sysctl in message #9, and sending signals to threads with htop in message #11. The design now mixes a signal handler, a self-pipe, a second thread and siglongjmp() out of fgets(). Message #12 calls this area hard to follow even before the patch. Message #12 also asks whether that siglongjmp() is safe with threads, and the thread gives no answer.
refuted.author_must_show: Which TAP tests exercise Ctrl+C through the new cancel thread in psql and in pg_dump parallel mode, so that later changes fail loudly?

critic.reasoning: psql already has a TAP test, 020_cancel.pl, that sends SIGINT to a running psql, so the basic cancel path through the new thread would be exercised on Unix. Wider test coverage is a level 4 matter, which the rubric puts out of scope.

refuted.title: Reshaped cancel.h API still fits only one connection per process
refuted.failure_scenario: Someone later moves Unix pg_dump workers to threads, the follow-up suggested in message #1, or adds per-client cancel to pgbench. The global cancelConn and one cancel thread cannot serve them, so cancel.c is redesigned again and every tool's call sites change a second time.
refuted.argument: The patch changes the fe_utils cancel API, including a new setup_cancel_handler() with two callbacks, but keeps one global connection. Message #4 raised this limit, and message #5 answered that it is scope creep. [P4] shows that multi-connection cancel in pgbench already failed on thread races, so the case is real. The more general designs in message #12 remain open.
refuted.author_must_show: How would the new cancel.h API extend to several connections in one process without another change at every call site?

precedents.title: pgbench: allow to cancel queries during benchmark

critic.reasoning: The single global cancelConn exists in cancel.c today, so the patch keeps existing practice; message #4 says it is fine for current callers and message #5 answers the scope question. [P4] failed on pgbench thread races and does not show this API is at fault.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: The tools now send cancel requests over an encrypted connection through the existing libpq cancel API; the protocol itself does not change.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The fe_utils cancel.h API changes, including a new setup_cancel_handler() with two callbacks, and pthread-win32.c moves to src/port.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: psql -f scripts exit with code 3 on Ctrl+C at input prompts, and the prompt can stay blocked on a stuck cancel connection.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The cancel key no longer travels in clear text when the session uses SSL or GSS.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Message #1 asks about a backport to PG17 and PG18 as a security fix; the thread has not settled it.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Every frontend tool gains a cancel thread, a self-pipe and a new configure and meson check for pselect().

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which platforms had the broken pselect() behind the revert in [P12], and are any of them still supported or in the buildfarm today?
What do the tools do when the cancel thread cannot be created, or on a platform without threads?
Is a second call to setup_cancel_handler() now guarded against, as raised in review?
Has cancel through a bad network been tested for tools other than psql, such as pg_dump with parallel workers?
Is the plan master-only, or is a backport to PG17 and PG18 still wanted?

committability.owner_note: Peter Eisentraut committed v13-0001 and is listed as reviewer; Heikki Linnakangas reviewed the design in depth. The owner needs to know frontend signal handling, threads and platform portability.
committability.liability: The owner signs for Ctrl+C behaviour in psql, pg_dump, pgbench and the scripts on every supported platform, including the signal handler, self-pipe, cancel thread and pselect() path, for as long as these tools exist.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted 13 versions over about 11 months, rebased repeatedly and answered review, which suggests continued follow-up.

priority.reason: Every SSL or GSS user of the frontend tools is affected, and committers are already engaged with one part committed. The remaining series changes signal and thread handling in many tools, so review is costly and the new cancel path needs ongoing care.

provisional_note: Without the code, the review could not check thread safety of siglongjmp() out of input waits, the wait in SetCancelConn() and ResetCancelConn() for an in-flight cancel, or the pselect() signal masking. Only 3 of 32 messages were visible, so later answers may exist.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Issue in postgres_fdw causing unnecessary wait for cancel request reply
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes postgres_fdw wait for a cancel reply only when a cancel request was actually sent, so that a NULL return from PQgetCancel() no longer causes a 30-second wait. It also adds error messages to PQgetCancel(), a WARNING in postgres_fdw when PQgetCancel() fails, an AF_UNIX check that skips TCP parameter parsing, and a shared parse function for the keepalives parameter.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding after review, and the CommitFest manager returned the entry with feedback while open issues remained. Jelte Fennema objected that PQgetCancel() should not set error messages on the connection object. Robert Haas objected to the AF_UNIX check because it skips sanity checks on invalid values such as tcp_user_timeout='a'.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I agree that we shouldn't try to *use* the values if they don't apply, but I'm not sure it's a good idea to skip *sanity-checking* them when they don't apply.

precedents_retrieved.title: Refactoring of connection with password prompt loop for frontends
precedents_retrieved.summary: Consolidate the repeated frontend pattern of connecting to the backend with a password-prompt retry loop (used in several client tools) into a single shared routine in src/fe_utils. The patch unified error handling across tools but left out pg_dumpall and the code paths that prompt for a password before the first connection attempt.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author marked it returned with feedback himself. Open design questions remained: an unresolved XXX comment, and the handling of tools (vacuumlo, scripts/common.c, pg_dump) that prompt for a password before the first connection or reuse it across connections. Resolving these needed further work to avoid password exposure hazards. The patch also drew little review attention.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
For now I am switching the patch as returned with feedback as there is
much more to consider.  And it did not attract much attention either.

precedents_retrieved.title: Extend comments on signal handling and cross-reference comments on signal handling functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: A comments-only patch expanded the signal handling section in miscadmin.h to cover ProcSignal and deferred signal handling during blocking calls. It also added cross-references between the main signal handling routines and that comment.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Mark Dilger pointed out that two new comments in interrupt.c contradict each other: one says normal user backends do not use its handlers, another says most backends use one of them. The author did not reply during two commitfests, so Daniel Gustafsson closed the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm closing this as Returned with Feedback as it there has been no response to
the review comment during two commitfests.

precedents_retrieved.title: pgbench: allow to cancel queries during benchmark
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pgbench send cancel requests to all connections on Ctrl+C, so long-running benchmark queries do not keep running on the backend after pgbench exits. On non-Windows, thread #0 handles SIGINT and cancels queries for all clients through a global array of client states.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fabien COELHO said thread #0 cancelling clients that other threads manage can cause race conditions, and asked that each thread cancel its own clients. In message #19 the author found two more problems: thread #0 cannot cancel anything once it leaves its loop, and with -C each thread recreates its PGcancel objects while thread #0 reads them. Alvaro Herrera then said commit 61461a300c1c, which deprecated PQcancel, requires the patch to be reworked. The author planned a redesign, but the visible messages show no new version.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Due to commit 61461a300c1c, this patch needs to be reworked.

precedents_retrieved.title: minor fix in CancelVirtualTransaction
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the loop in CancelVirtualTransaction to stop scanning once it finds the entry with the matching backendId, even when the localTransactionId does not match and no signal is sent. A later version compares backendId directly with the proc entry and adds a code comment, following review.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author paused the patch because the code has no test coverage and he wanted to write a test first. The test did not arrive, so Andres Freund marked the entry returned with feedback. The reviewer agreed with the change itself.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
However, now I realize that this code is not covered at all, so I'll put
this patch to sleep until I write some test for it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add "\gi file" to psql to allow COPY with variable expansion
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch first let psql's \copy expand :-variables in table and file names. After Tom Lane objected to the implementation, it became a new \gi file (or \gi command|) meta-command that sends a SQL COPY ... FROM STDIN with input from a file or program, and \copy was rewritten on top of the \g and \gi code.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The cfbot tests for the \gi patch failed for weeks, and the cfbot log included a core dump. Andres Freund reported this on 2025-05-13, and no fixed version was posted. He marked the entry returned with feedback on 2025-06-17.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: However, the tests have not passed in quite a while:

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump: optimize dumpFunc()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace pg_dump's per-function query in dumpFunc() with a single query that gathers data for all functions up front, keeping the PGresult in memory and using a sorted array of function OIDs to locate each function's row. The aim was to reduce dump time for databases with many functions (shown as about 0.25s to about 0.11s for 10k simple functions).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned whether the change helps databases with few functions and what it does to pg_dump's memory requirements when there are very many functions with large source text, and said the shown results did not justify the risk. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sure that the results you're showing justify taking any
risk here.

precedents_retrieved.title: Custom signals and handlers for extension
precedents_retrieved.authors: Maksim Milyutin (maksm90), Alexey Kondratov (ololobus), Pavel Borisov (pborisov)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets shared-preload extensions reserve custom ProcSignal slots from a fixed set and register handler functions for them. A backend can then send such a signal to another backend, where the handler runs at CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS, giving extensions like pg_query_state a low-level RPC mechanism without patching core.
precedents_retrieved.objection: In 2018 the author did not respond to review for weeks, then said he wanted to rework the design and could not finish for that release, so it was returned with feedback. In 2020 Michael Paquier objected to a revived version because it had no test module and no documentation. He also objected to the hardcoded limit of 64 custom signals and asked for a flexible registration of custom procsignals at shmem init time.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Second, it uses
a hardcoded custom number of signals of 64 instead of a flexible
design.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert ac22929a26, as well as the followup fix 113d3591b8. Because it broke
the assumption that the startup process waiting for the recovery conflict
on buffer pin should be waken up only by buffer unpin or the timeout enabled
in ResolveRecoveryConflictWithBufferPin(). It caused, for example,
SIGHUP signal handler or walreceiver process to wake that startup process
up unnecessarily frequently.

Additionally, add the comments about why that dedicated latch that
the reverted patch tried to get rid of should not be removed.

Thanks to Kyotaro Horiguchi for the discussion.

roaster_notes.note: No earlier attempt at the same idea is in the list. The only recorded reason that still applies is the pselect() portability revert.
From the standards angle, the series adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object or pg_dump output. The committed exit-code change was discussed and settled in messages #28 to #32.

The proposal changes only how frontend tools send a cancel request, using the libpq cancel API that already exists. It adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog or wire protocol state, and the cancel.h change is internal to fe_utils, not an extension ABI. Not checked without code: whether a pooler that accepts TLS connections handles TLS cancel requests the same way.

The proposal tightens security: cancel requests from the frontend tools would use the same SSL or GSS encryption as the session, where the cancel key now goes in clear text. It adds no privilege, role, server-side exposure or attack surface that an unprivileged user could reach. The cancel thread and the blocked prompt on a stuck cancel connection affect only the user's own client process. Backpatching to PG17 and PG18 is still open in the thread, but that is a scope decision rather than a security flaw. Without the code, I could not check how the tools behave when the encrypted cancel connection fails where a plain one would have worked, for example through a pooler.
Desirability is not in doubt: sending the cancel key in clear text is a real defect, and Heikki Linnakangas and Peter Eisentraut are engaged and own the area.

No existing feature, extension or option lets psql, pg_dump or vacuumdb send an encrypted cancel request today, so the need is not met another way. The patch builds on the existing libpq cancel API and the existing Windows cancel thread rather than adding a second mechanism.

The problem applies to every SSL or GSS user of psql, pg_dump, pgbench and the scripts, because these tools send the cancel key in clear text, and users have no workaround. The project already deprecated PQcancel for this reason (61461a300), and [P4] shows that change forcing rework elsewhere. Several committers are engaged, and one part is committed. Demand is not the weak point here.
